When traveling out of the country either call your cell phone provider and let them know where you are going and find out if they can provide a cheap plan to allow you to use your phone in your destination countries don't forget the data. or plan on buying a cheap phone or SIM card when you get there. I also try to get important numbers both put in my phone and written down in case my phone is lost, stolen or quits working. Make sure to either get a card from your hotel or write the address down as well.

Learn how to dial to and from the country you are going to and home. This may sound simple, but can get confusing. I also usually find the 1-800 equivalent for an ATT operator (One exists in every country I have been to) so that in an emergency you can get an English speaking operator and get a call placed either with a credit card or phone card to home, travel agent, embassy or whatever.

Let your bank know where you are going. I almost got stranded on a toll road in France because I had run out of Euros and my bank shut my debit card off. Luckily I was able to call and get it turned back on in a timely manner because I made sure my phone would work from there. I also usually keep emergency cash separate from the cash in my wallet.

Do not use the foreign exchanges in the airport. I have found I get a much better rate by just hitting up an ATM at my destination country. If I have too much foreign currency when I get home I just go to my bank and they will deposit into my account at a much better exchange rate than one of those booths in the airport. They are like the payday lenders of the traveling world.

I really want to get a Shadowrun game going and the only way to do that is to do it myself but I am way out of my depth. I've got core-books, passion, and a dice app. Where do I start? How do I do?
How does someone who has not had a pen-and-paper roleplaying experience in 13 years become a decent GM?

Are you looking for players, or just unsure of your rusty GMing abilities? Back when you did role-play, was it Shadowrun or some other game?

If you are trying to find random players to form a new group with, I recommend going to local gaming stores and asking the people that work there if there is a regular gaming meetup group (for example, Pathfinder and D&D play on Sundays at mine), and if not, ask if you can start one, or even just put up a flyer by their register stating you're looking for a few good players. I'm sure there are online avenues as well, if that's your preference.

If you have a group, but are unsure of your skills as a GM, stop sweating it and get the game going already. Seriously. Get a couple of very basic frameworks of "this is stuff the players can do if they want', even if it it means working from a module or even just blatantly plagiarizing some Shadowrun book or similar content. Nobody is going to care if you have some stumbling around to do before you get your footing, nobody is going to care if you're ripping off a story or game they already know themselves (provided you change enough to not bore them). At the end of the night, the only thing that matters is that everybody involved had a great time, and maybe got a good story because of it.

If you and your players are all new to Shadowrun, it might take a few nights and even a few "well, that sucked, let's start over" characters/stories before you get going, but it will sort itself out way quicker than you are worried it will. Shadowrun in particular is pretty well known for its, shall we say, need for several character creations per player per campaign, so even that isn't much of a hindrance if things kinda suck at first. Just get going and make sure every player is involved and having a good time.

RP for a bit as a player before starting your own campaign - it'll refresh your memory on what GMs can do that is good and what sucks. While you're doing this, assuming you can build some rapport with the other players, ask them what they like/dislike about the current GM or other GMs they've played with, and take that on board. If you feel comfortable with it, ask a GM if you can guest GM a night (most GMs I know would welcome a break and love to bring a one-time character into their own campaign for a bit of mischief).
